title: source file differs from the ledger row's source_sha256 -> NOT-VERIFIED(source-hash)
spec_case: V3: the source file's content no longer matches the ledger row's source_sha256 (edited after export). The vault copy still matches the row exactly. Expected: NOT-VERIFIED(source-hash).
path_convention: substitute @FIXTURE_ROOT@ with the ROOT printed by make-fixture.sh; make-fixture.sh also writes the substituted copy to <ROOT>/expected.json
ledger_header: source_path	source_sha256	vault_path	vault_sha256	exported_at	note
live_ledger_untouched: corpus/knowledge/obsidian-ledger.tsv stays header-only; the builder never writes it (test ledgers live under tests/vault/)

declared_ledger_rows.why: the row records the export-time bytes on both sides; the vault copy still carries them (digest matches), but the source file was edited afterwards (current digest bac6faf0...) — the source-side conjunct is the only failure

same shape as the primary target, but the source copy differs from the row's source_sha256 by exactly one byte (the dropped trailing newline; current digest 45d91bb2...): catches size- or mtime-based shortcuts and any non-byte-exact comparison
control row: both sides are byte-identical to the row's recorded digest, so a correct tool returns VERIFIED — proving the mismatch verdicts are not a blanket failure

expect.why: the source path exists and the vault path exists with a digest equal to the row's vault_sha256; the source file's sha256 (bac6faf0...) differs from the row's source_sha256 (655cb8c2...) — the source-side hash is the only failing conjunct. The exact list carries the bare class plus the sha/hash spelling aliases the r4 impls emit (source-hash-mismatch, source-sha-mismatch); contains 'source' is present in every accepted spelling and absent in wrong-side (vault-*) answers
same shape as the primary target but the source copy differs by exactly one byte (dropped trailing newline): a one-byte edit must flip the source-side conjunct
control: both paths exist and both digests equal the row's recorded values

accept.note: canonical token NOT-VERIFIED(source-hash); the contains fallback admits the hash/sha spelling variants the r4 impls emit (source-hash-mismatch, source-sha-mismatch). Case-level accept binds to the primary target only; the VERIFIED control and the subtle target carry their own per-target accept blocks.

must_not_be_note: the bare token VERIFIED is deliberately absent: harnesses apply must_not_be as a substring veto and 'VERIFIED' is a substring of the correct answer 'NOT-VERIFIED(source-hash)'; a false VERIFIED answer is still caught by the verdict-class comparison. The list is scoped to the primary target (must_not_be_applies_to) so its SAFE class-veto cannot fire against the VERIFIED control's correct answer, matching the V2 house pattern.
failure_modes_caught: vault-side-only verification: the vault file digest matches the row's vault_sha256, so a harness that skips the source hash check reports VERIFIED/SAFE — caught by expect.verdict
class collapse: reporting NOT-SAFE(none) or NOT-SAFE(unreachable) instead of the distinct NOT-VERIFIED(source-hash) — caught by expect.reason
false source-hash on a matching pair: the control target (byte-identical both sides) must be VERIFIED — a blanket source-hash answer fails the control

source_side.why: the file was edited in place after export; its current digest is the edited revision, not the row's export-time digest

vault_side.why: the vault copy still carries the export-time bytes, so its digest equals the row's vault_sha256 — the vault side verifies, the source side does not

build.git: git init -q -b master on <ROOT> (offline, no commits) so the fixture root behaves like a real repo
build.determinism: fixed content bytes; paths vary per run; every content digest and byte count is asserted at build time
build.safety: never reads or writes the live ledger, the real vault, or any sibling repo; writes only under --out (plus --ledger FILE when given)

crosscheck.note: the r2 tool tools/souji-verify.sh predates the r4 VERIFIED vocabulary; for the primary target its expected output is the same verdict class under r2 names
crosscheck.expected_line: VERDICT	<ROOT>/source/src/edited-notes.md	NOT-SAFE	none	pushed=...; obsidian=source-sha-mismatch; obsidian=no-matching-ledger-row; stale=...
crosscheck.control: the same tool with the same ledger must report SAFE/moved-to-obsidian for <ROOT>/source/src/matched-notes.md

notes: The builder writes ONLY: <FIXTURE_ROOT>/** and, when --ledger FILE is given, FILE. The live ledger and the real vault /home/vgpnk/Documents/shokoknowledge are never touched; this case is self-contained under tests/vault/.
The vault here is a fake vault dir under the fixture root — no Obsidian process, no CLI, no network is involved.
stdout contract: line 1 = JSON {case,root,ledger,targets,expect}; then FIXTURE_READY case-V3 <ROOT>; then KEY=VALUE lines; --quiet emits the FIXTURE_READY + KEY=VALUE lines only.
Exit codes: 0 built (also for --print-*), 1 build/assertion failure, 2 usage.
